basis.ref: Introduced as the Profile cutoff set in commit 790efee (2026-07-21, 'Add auditable TREC evaluation profiles'), whose message lists 'nDCG and label-at-least-1 precision at cutoffs 5, 10, and 20' while 'preserving legacy metrics'. The earlier harness had one cutoff, METRIC_CUTOFF = 5 (commit fee684d), so only 5 has an earlier source; 10 was later named the primary endpoint (nDCG@10). Nothing records why 10 and 20 joined, or why recall is emitted only at these cutoffs when the frozen protocol of 2026-08-29 (section 7.2) requires judged eligible recall at 100, 500 and 1,000. Searched: git log -S across every branch for the value in each spelling, the introducing commits' messages, the ADRs, protocols, specs and reporting policy.

basis.ref: ADR 0002 (evaluation and comparison contract): 'NIST judgments retain their original meanings' and 'The primary reporting metric is macro-averaged graded nDCG@10 with linear gains 0, 1, and 2.' The gain function in taim.evaluation has carried the same rule since the first harness (commit fee684d): 'TREC Clinical Trials uses the judgment label directly as graded gain: eligible=2, condition-relevant-but-excluded=1, and not relevant=0.' The Profile schema admits no other mapping.
